jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Ghosting the Ghost
jokes.joke: I paid a psychic to contact my dead grandfather. She closed her eyes and said, "He's here. He wants you to stop wasting money." I lost my temper. I said, "I paid you eighty bucks to get yelled at by a dead man?" She said, "Actually, he says you still owe him twenty."

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Séance Etiquette
jokes.joke: I went on a ghost tour last month. The guide says, ‘Stay calm, spirits feed on fear.’ Then a floorboard creaked and I screamed so loud I lost the group. Now I’m the only haunting that tour has. Somewhere there’s a ghost telling his friends, ‘Some guy’s still down in the cellar yelling at me, and I’m the one who’s dead.’

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Maestro's Macchiato
jokes.joke: I saw an orchestra conductor lose his temper at a barista today. It’s impossible to be intimidated by a guy whose default angry body language is waving an imaginary wand. He's screaming about his cold macchiato, but his hands are aggressively keeping a 4/4 time signature. Like, calm down, man, you're not threatening anyone. You just look like you’re about to cue the brass section to emphasize your disappointment in oat milk.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Ghost Passengers
jokes.joke: I was on the late subway when the conductor came over the intercom and said, "Next stop is haunted—keep your arms inside and ignore any floating tickets." I laughed until a translucent guy sat down next to me and asked if the seat was taken. I said yes. He vanished. The conductor just nodded like it was a regular Tuesday.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Executive Presence
jokes.joke: I work in a supposedly haunted office. Everyone kept reporting a ghost in the CEO's office, so management brought in a paranormal expert. After one hour he said, 'Good news, it's not a spirit.' Apparently no dead person would spend that much time in the building and still ask why profits are down.

scores.comment: Clear premise and an amusing reversal in which the ghost becomes the frightened party. The final line is slightly overexplained, weakening the punch. Entertaining but not especially memorable.

Strong visual comedy built around a conductor's involuntary gestures. The 4/4 detail adds specificity, and the brass-section punchline delivers a satisfying escalation. Slightly wordy, but genuinely funny.

Understandable supernatural scenario, but the ghost politely disappearing has little comic force. The conductor's indifference is predictable, and the ending supplies atmosphere rather than a punchline.

Recognizable workplace satire with a coherent supernatural setup. The CEO's obsession with profits offers a mild payoff, but the corporate caricature is familiar and the punchline lacks a sharp, unexpected turn.

Clear stage premise and a real turn: the dead grandfather’s money complaint flips into him collecting a debt. Natural rhythm, and the last line carries the laugh. The psychic-contacts-dead-relative setup is familiar, which limits originality.

Good observational image of a conductor’s hands keeping time mid-rant. The middle works, but the ending explains the joke instead of snapping. ‘Calm down, man’ and the repeated point dilute the final beat. Oat milk is a soft closer.

Subway ‘conductor’ is a loose reading, and the haunted-ride premise is vague. ‘Seat taken? Yes. He vanished’ is mildly cute but the ghost reacts to nothing funny. The ending (‘regular Tuesday’) is a stock deadpan closer with no turn.

The turn that the CEO is worse than a ghost has a decent kernel, but ‘profits are down’ is a generic office-satire beat. The logic is muddled: it’s unclear why no spirit would linger, and the last sentence is overlong and explains itself rather than landing cleanly.
Classic misdirection with a sharp, well-executed punchline and natural stage dialogue.
Strong premise shift where the comic becomes the haunting; good stage rhythm and button.
Reads more like a whimsical story than a stand-up bit, lacking a concrete punchline to carry the laugh.
Competent execution but relies heavily on a standard workplace trope rather than discovering a fresh angle.
Clean setup-to-punch with a satisfying money-still-owed snap; familiar psychic frame elevated by the second demand.
Clear premise but the payoff stretches and softens; the ghost’s complaint feels more narrative than sharp stand-up.
Strong visual incongruity of angry 4/4 conducting; specific, stage-ready image that lands cleanly.
Efficient corporate-paranormal twist; solid smile but the final line doesn’t fully escalate the laugh.
Clear setup and payoff. The extra debt reveal is a solid tag, though the psychic/grandparent angle feels familiar.
Good escalation from fear to accidentally becoming the haunting. Strong image and a clean final turn.
Funny observational premise sustained with specific details. Oat milk tag works, though the central joke arrives early.
Readable and coherent, but more of a whimsical paranormal scenario than a joke with a strong punchline or turn.
